What was tried (round 3, on the 64B wide-node tree): instead of filling the TriData buffer up front in OBJ order and storing the original triangle id in each leaf payload, the builder appended each triangle's TriData at leaf-emission time (depth-first), so the payload became the new slot index and spatially neighbouring leaves indexed adjacent triangle records. BuildState gained a tri_data pointer, the leaf branch of BuildWideNode pushed and emitted `slot | LEAF_BIT`, and the degenerate n==1 root path was fixed to append its triangle too (one compile error there — a stale `tri` reference — which I fixed).

What it measured, same-session interleaved A/B vs scratch/wideA (identical wide-node source, random/original TriData order), scene-default 512x512/64spp, --threads 8 --seed 1:
